 Foxconn Unveils Three New EV Reference Designs: The Rugged MODEL A+, City Pop-Inspired MODEL K+, and MODEL K Mini-Truck
 Aggressive Push into Japan: Right-Hand Drive MODEL B Debuts as EV Lineup Expands to 12 Models

 2026-10-30 💡 Key Takeaways Core Highlight 1: Foxconn has unveiled three new reference design EVs—the MODEL A+, MODEL K+, and MODEL K—bringing its CDMS portfolio to 12 models, covering everything from Japanese K-cars to luxury off-road SUVs.
 Core Highlight 2: On the technical front, the vehicles introduce "In-Wheel Motor" technology and flexible E/E architecture. The MODEL A+ features high wading depth and emergency power supply capabilities, while the MODEL K+ focuses on "New City Pop" retro aesthetics and high spatial customization.
 Core Highlight 3: Accelerating international deployment, Foxconn showcased the "Right-Hand Drive MODEL B" for the first time, demonstrating full vertical integration from battery cells and BMS to powertrain systems, targeting RHD markets in Japan and Southeast Asia.
 During the grand finale of the Hon Hai Tech Day 2026 (HHTD26) main stage this morning (Oct 30), following progress updates from executives at Honda R&D and Mitsubishi Electric Mobility (MEM)—which is set to merge into Foxconn in October 2027—Foxconn EV Chief Strategy Officer Jun Seki personally led the reveal of three new reference design EVs. These models target “blue ocean” markets where EV penetration remains low, featuring designs that pay homage to Japanese culture: the luxury off-road “MODEL A+,” the “New City Pop” retro lifestyle SUV “MODEL K+,” and the “MODEL K” electric pickup, aimed at Japan’s K-car light commercial segment.
 With the addition of these three newcomers, Foxconn’s Contract Design and Manufacturing Service (CDMS) portfolio has officially surpassed 12 reference models since the debut of its first prototype six years ago (2020). The exhibition floor also featured the first public display of the “Right-Hand Drive MODEL B,” a symbol of CDMS localization in Japan and other RHD markets, alongside a showcase of vertical integration capabilities spanning battery materials, cells, modules, BMS, E/E architecture, and powertrains for two- and three-wheel EVs.
 Deep Dive into Three New EVs: “In-Wheel Motor” Tech from Luxury Off-Roading to Japanese K-Cars 
 Jun Seki noted that these three new vehicles aim to help traditional automakers and cross-sector B2B customers accelerate time-to-market and reduce development costs through highly flexible modular platforms and cost-competitive options, specifically targeting niche markets often overlooked by mass-market manufacturers:
 “MODEL A+”: A Hardcore Off-Road SUV with In-Wheel Motors, Wading Capabilities, and Luxury Glamping Features 
 Platform Positioning and Design: Built on the modular B-segment foundations of the previously released MODEL A, this vehicle is designed for the growing high-value global SUV market, blending rugged off-road DNA with a premium, high-tech cabin.
 Core Technical Highlights: 
 In-Wheel Motor Technology and Optional E/E Architecture (EEA): By integrating the powertrain directly into the wheels, Foxconn has freed up significant chassis and cabin space while enabling precise independent four-wheel torque control for superior off-road recovery.
 Disaster Relief Wading and Mobile Living: The vehicle boasts exceptional wading depth for extreme weather or emergency scenarios. Its spacious cabin and high-capacity V2L (Vehicle-to-Load) capabilities allow it to serve as a temporary living space or backup power station, catering to the “Vanlife” and luxury glamping lifestyle.
 “MODEL K+”: An Affordable, Retro-Chic SUV Honoring Japan’s “New City Pop” Aesthetic 
 Platform Positioning and Design: Targeted at vibrant young consumers and lifestyle brands, the design team used modern techniques to reconstruct nostalgic elements, infusing the body lines with Japan’s classic “City Pop” urban retro trend to create a highly recognizable and affordable compact SUV.
 Core Technical Highlights: 
 Rare In-Wheel Motors + Full Customization: Also utilizing in-wheel motor technology to maximize interior space, the MODEL K+ offers high levels of customization for exterior styling, interior layout, battery range, and E/E architecture. This addresses the pain point of traditional mass production being unable to handle low-volume, high-variety personalized demands, helping B2B brands launch differentiated EVs at competitive prices.
 “MODEL K”: A Versatile Commercial Platform Targeting Japan’s Iconic “Kei-Truck” Segment 
 Platform Positioning and Design: Foxconn is officially extending its electric mobility footprint into Japan’s most ubiquitous vehicle segment: the K-car (Kei-car) mini-truck. The exterior balances futurism with extreme utilitarianism.
 Core Application Scenarios: 
 Versatile Bed Modifications and Low TCO: Featuring a highly practical chassis and body layout, the rear bed can be flexibly adapted for various commercial services—from last-mile e-commerce delivery and mobile cafes to carbon-neutral government fleets or emergency “mobile power stations.” This significantly reduces energy consumption and maintenance costs for small business owners.
 Bonus Reveal: Right-Hand Drive MODEL B Appears as CDMS Partnership Enters Harvest Phase 
 Beyond the concept cars on the main stage, two other key highlights at the Taipei exhibition underscored Foxconn’s EV commercialization progress:
 Right-Hand Drive MODEL B Debut: A production-spec RHD version of the MODEL B crossover was showcased, tailored for markets like Japan, Southeast Asia, Australia, and the UK, allowing guests to see the tangible results of Foxconn’s CDMS partnerships with international clients.
 Full “Battery & E/E Vertical Integration”: Echoing Chairman Young Liu’s opening remarks on “full lifecycle battery manufacturing and recycling,” the EV zone displayed Foxconn’s self-developed battery materials, cells, packs, and BMS, alongside next-gen E/E architecture and powertrains for electric two- and three-wheelers developed for emerging Asian markets.
